text: Old Henry looked like a tired farmer.
That was what people were meant to see.
But trouble had a way of finding men like Henry, even when they hid well.
Henry lived with his boy on land that did not give much back.
They worked it anyway.
They fed the animals, fixed what broke, and kept their heads down.
The boy wanted more.
He did not.
Henry brought the wounded man inside, and the boy watched, full of questions.
Henry answered few of them.
Like a man remembering.
The riders came with dust behind them.
They looked like lawmen at first.
He did not invite them in.
The man in front did most of the talking.
He said they were looking for a thief.
Said the wounded man inside had stolen money.
Said Henry would be smart to hand him over.
That was the wrong answer, and everyone on the porch knew it.
The riders left for that time, but they did not leave far.
Henry watched them go and knew they would be back.
"Men choose.".
The attack came after dark.
That was no surprise.
Something else had stood up.
The first man came through the door too fast.
Henry dropped him before his second boot cleared the frame.
The second tried the window.
Henry turned and fired once.
He had been hiding because he was dangerous.
The leader called from outside.
He tried threats first.
Maybe he was.
By morning, the farm had changed.
The riders were down.
Now he had one.
Henry walked into the yard with his rifle low and his eyes tired.
The leader was still alive enough to know who had beaten him.
Then recognition came.
Not all at once.
Just finished.
The farm went quiet again, but not the same quiet as before.
The boy knew now that his father was not small.
The dust settled, and justice was still standing.
